request.deadline: instantly performed as part of the governance action's enactment on-chain
deliverables: Instant on-chain distribution of funds to the intended recipient upon governance action enactment
request.recipient: the Ikigai Info governance action submitter / intended recipient, not otherwise named in document
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to reimburse the lost deposit for the Ikigai Info governance action and compensate estimated missed staking rewards.

claims.claim: An Info governance action titled "Cardanoの生きがい - Ikigai -" was submitted in September 2024 shortly after the Chang hard fork.
The Ikigai Info governance action was symbolic and asked the community whether they agreed with a statement of thanks and hope for Cardano's future.
A Cardano node bug permitted an unregistered stake key to be used in the governance action, preventing the submitter from recovering a 100000 ADA deposit.
The Cardano community expressed sentiment at the time that the Ikigai Info governance action deposit should be reimbursed via treasury withdrawal.
No entity-based budget submission included the reimbursement after treasury withdrawals became available following the Plomin hard fork.
The Cardano in Oceania initiative included the reimbursement in its budget Info governance action, but that governance action was not approved.
The requested withdrawal is 103000 ADA, consisting of the original 100000 ADA deposit plus 3000 ADA for lost staking rewards calculated at 2% per annum.
The proposal states there are no costs or expenses associated with the withdrawal and no circumstances under which funds would be refunded to the treasury.
The proposal states the recipient has not previously received treasury funds.
The proposal provides an external governance reference URI for the original action on adastat.net.

summary: The proposal asks for 103000 ADA to reimburse an alleged unrecoverable 100000 ADA governance deposit plus estimated missed staking rewards, with instant on-chain delivery to the intended recipient and limited supporting evidence beyond assertions and one external governance reference.
